game: The Last of Us Part II
observations: The game groups accessibility presets while allowing individual options to be adjusted.
Navigation assistance, traversal cues, combat audio cues, enhanced listen mode, high-contrast display, text-to-speech, and vibration cues provide different routes to actionable state.
Options can alter presentation, input, information, or assistance and therefore are not semantically interchangeable.
inferences: A useful accessibility test compares objective and disclosed assistance effects rather than visual sameness.
Presets reduce setup burden but cannot replace testing the composed individual configuration.
limits: The official list does not expose internal event binding or exhaustive option-interaction results.
Player-specific barriers require testing beyond feature presence.
